clue.text: Methane discharged by power unit

parts.note: a gun discharged has been fired
the amp is the unit of electric current, here loosely a power unit

explanation.surface: Gas released by an electrical generator.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the miners' name for the explosive methane gas found in coal pits.

clue.text: Having no effect for patient

definitions.meaning: a contract with no effect is void, not valid
a patient is someone ill and under care

explanation.surface: Something ineffective being prescribed for a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it means void or ineffective; on the first, a sick person is an invalid or patient.

clue.text: Former monarch had up about speed is offhand

indicators.note: about means the outer pieces go around the next part

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, had up means the word for the monarch is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword monarch
tempo is the speed of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A deposed king hauled into court over his speeding, speaking off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had up' (in a down light, turned upwards) reverses the monarch; 'about' wraps the former-monarch letters around the musical speed. 'offhand' here means impromptu, not rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore speech is improvised, given offhand without preparation.

clue.text: So-called spirit is imaginary

indicators.note: so-called means the spirit's name as it is called out, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: Ariel is the airy spirit in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A supposed ghost is only a figment of the imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial in its literary sense means airy, insubstantial, existing only in fancy.

clue.text: Grace, for example — one may stand for it, naturally

definitions.text: Grace, for example — one may stand for it, naturally

parts.words: Grace, for example — one may stand for it, naturally
parts.note: a person, naturally, may stand for an abstract quality such as grace, embodying it in human form

explanation.surface: Someone named Grace naturally stands for that virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Personification is representing an abstract quality such as grace as a person.

clue.text: Contradict female opinion

parts.note: to belie something is to contradict or give the lie to it

explanation.surface: Arguing against a woman's view.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief is a view or conviction one holds, an opinion.

clue.text: It could be bad one if it's on the level

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something might seem a bad one even though it is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: BADONEIF rearranged gives the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide means genuine, in good faith, and on the level is an idiom for honest.

clue.text: Worship that is holding solid for a change

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the next

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: for a change means the word solid is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A devotee clings firmly to something for the sake of variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' scrambles SOLID to DOLIS, which 'holding' wraps in the abbreviation for id est; 'Worship' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to worship or adore them excessively.

clue.text: One of the points at which things are very familiar

definitions.text: One of the points at which things are very familiar

parts.words: One of the points at which things are very familiar
parts.note: a knowledgeable person has facts at the tips of the hand's digits, the place where well-known things sit

explanation.surface: A riddle about where well-known things are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is having knowledge 'at your fingertips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar knowledge is said to be at one's fingertips, so a single tip of a digit is such a point.

clue.text: Archetype for a tank a Russian leader wanted

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Russian

explanation.surface: A Soviet commander demanding a tank as the model of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is an embodiment or archetypal incarnation of an idea.

clue.text: Dashes to the ground and searches successfully

definitions.meaning: to run someone down is to knock them over with a vehicle
to run down a quarry is to track it and find it

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting downhill to find what they lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both knocking someone over and finally tracking something down after a search.

clue.text: Backache apparent after beginning to process lead

indicators.note: after puts the backache word behind the first letter
beginning to means take the first letter of the word process

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A back pain shows up when someone starts working with lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black lead of pencils.

clue.text: Like a leopard, say, viewing iron bar

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a bar is a line or stripe

explanation.surface: A leopard pacing behind the iron bars of its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means belonging to the cat family, as the leopard does.

clue.text: I had written most of letter in Greek for Charlie

parts.note: I had, as written in contracted form, is I'd

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the Greek letter is dropped

parts.note: iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone writing a Greek letter to a man named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims IOTA to IOT. Charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie in British slang is a fool, a synonym for a dimwit.

clue.text: In time to change trains during journey

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to change means the letters of trains are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arriving just in time to switch trains mid-trip.
explanation.definitionFit: In transit means on the way, while travelling during a journey.

clue.text: Search for eggs in the soup

definitions.meaning: to go looking for wild birds' eggs is the verb ...
the edible nest of the swiftlet goes into a famous Chinese soup

explanation.surface: Hunting for eggs only to land in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble; it is the ingredient of the Chinese delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hunting for eggs; as a noun it is the swiftlet's nest that goes into the soup.

clue.text: One at your side whom you may force into beggary

definitions.meaning: a person living next to you

definitions.text: whom you may force into beggary
definitions.meaning: the card game and trade policy beggar-my-... impoverishes the person next door

explanation.surface: The person beside you whom you could ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Beggar-my-neighbour is a card game, and a policy that enriches oneself at others' cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living or sitting next to you is a neighbour, the victim in beggar-my-neighbour.

clue.text: Well-controlled in concert

definitions.meaning: an informal sense of being composed and self-possessed

explanation.surface: A disciplined orchestra playing in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a composed person is together; jointly or in unison is also together.

clue.text: Like a dirge on ditcher's downfall

indicators.note: downfall means the letters of on and ditcher collapse into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A mournful song sung at the collapse of a ditch-digger.
explanation.walkthrough: ONDITCHER rearranged gives the adjective from threnody.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge, so threnodic means having the character of one.

clue.text: Pair starting off where packs meet for hunt

indicators.note: pair starting off means the first two letters are removed

parts.note: in rugby the two packs of forwards meet in a scrummage

explanation.surface: Two hounds leaving where the packs gather for the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' suggests hounds; they are rugby forwards. A scrummage (scrum) is where the two teams' forwards lock together.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things searching untidily.

clue.text: Girl who goes to the wall

definitions.text: Girl who goes to the wall

parts.words: Girl who goes to the wall
parts.note: the idiom for failing hides a picture of a glamour poster fixed on a wall

explanation.surface: A girl who fails or gets pushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to the wall' means fails, but here literally a picture pinned on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a photo of an attractive woman, or the woman herself, fixed to a wall.

clue.text: Removes domino and lays oneself open

definitions.meaning: a domino is a small eye mask worn at masquerades

explanation.surface: A masquerade guest takes off the disguise and becomes vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domino' here is a masquerade mask, not the game tile.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask is to take off a mask and also to reveal or expose.

clue.text: Drunk — one ousted by a university and given a lesson

indicators.note: ousted by means the one is replaced by what follows

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drunk student thrown out by a university after being taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousted by' swaps the I in TIGHT for AU.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught is the past participle of teach, so taught means given a lesson.

clue.text: Respect maiden in a desperate situation

indicators.note: in means the maiden goes inside the following words

parts.note: dire means desperate, as in dire straits
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Admiring a young woman in a hopeless plight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl; in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs, M.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to respect or esteem them.

clue.text: Alcoholics admit phony anthem is an abomination

indicators.note: admit means the first piece lets the other into its middle

parts.note: AA stands for Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: phony means the letters of anthem are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: Recovering drinkers confess that a fake national song is loathsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phony' scrambles the song into NATHEM, which 'admit' lets inside the recovering drinkers' fellowship; 'Alcoholics' alone stands for the whole organisation's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anathema is detested, an abomination or object of loathing.

clue.text: Port once used to drug sailors, possibly

definitions.meaning: a major seaport city in China
to press men into a ship's crew, often by drugging them, was once called this

explanation.surface: A harbour once notorious for drugging seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the name; the verb arose from the port's crimps.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large Chinese seaport, and as a verb it means to kidnap men for a crew, often by drugging.

clue.text: Grey river bird

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A grey bird by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The grouse is a game bird of the moors.

clue.text: Slight earthquake knocking capital right back

indicators.note: back means the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A quake knocking the Italian capital backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ROME + RT, ROMERT, as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking of the earth, a minor quake.

clue.text: Stateless ecologist, one barely feeling comfortable

indicators.note: Stateless means a state's abbreviation is removed, here Alabama's AL

parts.note: a naturalist studies nature, as an ecologist does

explanation.surface: An ecologist without a country feels at home in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is a nudist, someone comfortable wearing nothing at all.
